## The one distinction that matters

"Has a documented list of values" and "rejects values outside that list" are
independent properties, and this API separates them sharply.

29 enums are written into the contract: the wire will refuse anything else, so a
closed dropdown is safe.

3 are catalogs of values observed in live branch data against fields the contract
types as plain strings — `Opportunity.status`, `Category.categoryName`. They look
exactly like enums and are documented next to them, but nothing enforces them. A
closed dropdown here breaks the first time the branch adds a pipeline stage.

A further 19 fields sit in the same position with smaller or undocumented catalogs.
Every one of them is listed under [Soft enums](#soft-enums-string-on-the-wire-constrained-in-practice).

## Choosing a control

| Control | Options | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `radio` | ≤ 3 | ≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them |
| `select` | ≤ 12 | 4–12 options — a plain dropdown is scannable at a glance |
| `combobox` | ≤ 60 | 13–60 options — needs type-to-filter, but the full list is still renderable |
| `typeahead` | > 60 | >60 options — filter-as-you-type only; never render the full list |

Two things override the count. A free-text field needs a creatable control however
short its catalog. And `AssetLiabilityType` — four values, nominally a `select` —
decides which half of the form exists rather than recording a choice, so it is
worth treating as a mode switch rather than a field.

### CountryCode

**Country** · 250 values · suggested control `typeahead`

Enforced by the contract. Carried by `Address.country`.

_>60 options — filter-as-you-type only; never render the full list_

> ⚠️ 250 codes — typeahead only.
>
> ⚠️ It is not the current ISO 3166-1 list: `AN` (Netherlands Antilles, withdrawn 2010) is present. Validating user input against a live ISO library will reject values Mercury itself accepts and returns.

> ⚠️ The original Swagger had Norway's `NO` parsed as the boolean `false` (unquoted YAML). This live-audited contract has it fixed — but any client generated from the older spec still carries the bug.

**Gender** · 2 values · suggested control `radio`

Enforced by the contract. Carried by `Contact.gender`, `RelatedParty.gender`.

_≤3 options — show them all, no click to discover them_

> ⚠️ The wire contract admits exactly `M` and `F`. There is no non-binary, other, or undisclosed value, so a form cannot offer one — anything else is rejected. - `F`

### LoanStatusActive

**Pipeline stage (active)** · 27 values · suggested control `creatable-select`

**Not enforced by the contract** — a catalog of live values for `Opportunity.status`, which is typed as a plain string. Render it creatable.

_Overrides the 27-option default (`combobox`): the field this describes is free text on the wire, so the control has to accept values outside the list._

> ⚠️ Not an API constraint. `Opportunity.status` is a free-text string in the contract; these 27 values are the branch's live pipeline catalog. A closed dropdown here will block a legitimate value the moment the branch adds a stage — offer the known list, allow free text.
>
> ⚠️ Five values contain an en-dash (`–`), not a hyphen: `1. Lead – Discovery`, `8.2 Settled – Commission Paid`, `8.3 Construction Loan – Progress Payments`, `9.3/9.4/9.5 Mortgage Review – NN Month`. Retyping them with a hyphen produces a string that will not match.
>
> ⚠️ The leading numbers order the pipeline but do not sort lexically (`10` would fall between `1.` and `2.`); sort on an explicit index, not the label.
>

## Soft enums — string on the wire, constrained in practice

The contract types each of these as a plain string, so nothing rejects an
unexpected value. Offer the known values; keep the control creatable.

| Field | Control | Known values | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Opportunity.status` | `creatable-select` | _from `LoanStatusActive`, `LoanStatusInactive`_ | Free text in the contract; 30 branch pipeline values in live data. See the en-dash and sort-order hazards on LoanStatusActive. |
| `Category.categoryName` | `creatable-multiselect` | _from `FinhubContactCategoryName`_ | Free text in the contract; 15 branch values in three PREF-/FREQ-/REVIEW- families. Multi-valued via Contact.categories[]. |
| `Contact.citizenshipCountry` | `creatable-typeahead` | _from `CountryCode`_ | Typed `CountryCode \| string` in the generated types and plain string in the contract — offer the country list, accept anything. |
| `Contact.countryOfResidency` | `creatable-typeahead` | _from `CountryCode`_ | As above. |
| `Contact.companyRegisteredIn` | `creatable-typeahead` | _from `CountryCode`_ | As above. |
| `OpportunityExtensionRecord.key` | `select` | `livingExpense`, `otherIncome` | Determined by the route you called, not chosen by a user — it should not be an editable control at all. |
| `OpportunityExtensionRecord.parentType` | `hidden` | `loan` | Only `loan` observed. Constant, not a choice. |
| `LivingExpenseLineItem.type` | `creatable-select` | `Clothing & Personal Care`, `Child & Spouse Maintenance` | Open union — only two values documented, and the extension routes validate nothing. Offer what's known; expect more. |
| `OtherIncomeLineItem.type` | `creatable-select` | _from `IncomeType`_ | Open union that borrows IncomeType's vocabulary without its validation. |
| `Employment.employmentBasis` | `creatable-select` | `Full time`, `Part time` | Free text. Note the casing differs from EmploymentStatusContact's `Full Time` / `Part Time` — same words, different capitalisation, different field. |
| `Employment.employmentStatus` | `creatable-select` | `Primary`, `Secondary`, `Previous` | Free text, and NOT the same vocabulary as Contact.employmentStatus. See the collision note on EmploymentStatusContact. |
| `Employment.employmentType` | `creatable-select` | `Payg`, `Self employment` | Free text. |
| `Employment.paygEmployerType` | `creatable-select` | `Public`, `Private` | Free text. |
| `Address.type` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Residence type, free text with no documented value set — a plain text input is the honest control until live values are censused. |
| `Asset.propertyType` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Free text; no documented value set. |
| `Asset.propertyStatus` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Free text; no documented value set. |
| `Asset.propertyTitleType` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Free text; no documented value set. |
| `Asset.realEstateFinanceType` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Free text; no documented value set. |
| `Asset.motorVehicleType` | `creatable-select` | _none documented_ | Free text; no documented value set. |

## Field hazards that aren't enums

A form gets these wrong regardless of how well it handles the value sets.

### webpassword never render · critical

Observed in GET responses. Strip it at the wire boundary: never bind it to a control, never log it, never put it in client state. It should not exist in any model a UI can reach.

**Affects:** `Contact.webPassword`

### date epoch or string · high

Typed `number \| string` — live payloads return Unix epoch milliseconds where the original spec promised a date-time string. A date control must normalise on read (`typeof v === 'number' ? new Date(v) : new Date(String(v))`); passing an epoch number to a string date parser yields Invalid Date silently.

**Affects:** `Contact.createdOn`, `Contact.lastUpdated`, `Contact.deletedOn`, `Contact.dateOfBirth`, `Opportunity.createdOn`, `Opportunity.lastUpdated`, `Opportunity.statusLastUpdated`, `Opportunity.deletedOn`, `Opportunity.submittedToLenderDate`, `ContactMethod.modified`, `RelatedParty.dateOfBirth`

### boolean as string · medium

Typed `boolean \| string` — Mercury sometimes serialises it as the string `"true"`. A checkbox bound straight to it treats `"false"` as truthy.

**Affects:** `Opportunity.isNCCPEnabled`

### amount as string · high

String, not number — unlike every other money field in the API (`Expense.amount`, `Income.amount`, `Asset.value` are all numbers). A shared money input must serialise back to a string on these two.

**Affects:** `LivingExpenseLineItem.amount`, `OtherIncomeLineItem.amount`

### casing duplicates · high

The same concept ships under two casings depending on the endpoint. `Contact.Identification` (capital I) is the Swagger name; live Contact payloads use `identifications`. Read both, write the one the endpoint you are calling expects, and never let a form bind to only one.

**Affects:** `ContactMethod.personID`, `Income.personID`, `Income.personId`, `Expense.personID`, `Identification.personId`, `RelatedParty.personID`, `Address.parentId`, `Address.parentID`, `Contact.Identification`, `Contact.identifications`

### readonly hydrated fields · medium

Returned by GET as display/hydrated values. `Asset.motorVehicleMake` in particular is display-only — the make is written through `Asset.details`. Render these read-only; an editable control produces an edit that is silently discarded.

**Affects:** `Asset.motorVehicleMake`, `RelatedParty.fullName`, `RelatedParty.addressBlock`, `RelatedParty.email`, `RelatedParty.mobile`, `RelatedParty.dateOfBirth`, `Contact.fullName`, `Contact.dateOfBirthDisplay`, `Opportunity.lenderDisplayName`, `Opportunity.agentName`, `Opportunity.confirmedSettlementDateDisplay`, `Opportunity.nextActionDisplay`

### field name typo is the contract · medium

Missing the `l` in `Vehicle`. It is the real wire name — correcting the spelling in a client sends a field Mercury ignores.

**Affects:** `Asset.motorVehiceYear`

### extension put full replace · critical

A JSON-encoded string, not structured JSON, and its PUT is a destructive full replace. A form editing one line item must parse the string, merge, re-stringify and submit the complete array — anything omitted is deleted without warning.

**Affects:** `OpportunityExtensionRecord.value`

### collection reads require search · high

`search=true` is required on collection reads; `count` (default 100) and `offset` (default 0) drive pagination. A list view that omits `search` gets an error, not an empty page.

**Affects:** `GET /{token}/opportunities`, `GET /{token}/contacts`

## What this does not establish

The census behind the contract was read-only, so the following are still open and
need sandbox write probes before a form can rely on them:

- **Requiredness.** No schema declares `required`. Which fields a create call actually demands is unknown.
- **Writability.** Read-only vs request-only flags are unverified; the display-only fields listed under [field hazards](#readonly-hydrated-fields--medium) were inferred from response shape, not from a rejected write.
- **Validation boundaries.** String lengths, numeric ranges and date bounds are undocumented.
- **Create/update and soft-delete semantics** beyond the nested-entity PUT convention.
- **Pagination limits** — `count` defaults to 100; the ceiling is unconfirmed.
- **Nested item shapes** for `valueObjectOwnershipList`, `otherLoanPeople` and `assetLiabilityLinks`, which were empty in every sampled record.

`Contact.webPassword` was observed in GET responses. Redact it at the wire
boundary; it should not exist in any model a UI can reach.
